sentences.text: This appeal has been filed under section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 against the award dated 10.03.2024 passed in claim case No.710/2019 challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The issue of accident and liability of insurance company are not under dispute.
3. The facts giving rise to the case are that on 18.06.2018, the appellant was going along with his father on his Activa registration No.MP09-SK- 4078.
He was sitting as a pillion rider.

When they reached near Midland Dhaba, Near Pump, AB Road, Dewasnaka, Indore, the respondent No.2 came driving Truck No.MP09-HH-1747 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the vehicle of the appellant from behind because of which both of them fell down and truck crushed both the legs of the appellant.
The appellant suffered fracture below the left knee of his leg.
His femur bon of 2 MA-3189-2024 right thigh was also fractured.
The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the aforesaid accident.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence awarded a total sum of Rs.12,05,000/-to the appellant.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that at the time of the accident the appellant was 22 years of age and he was working in M/s CRM Services India Private Limited as a customer care executive.
He was earning Rs.1,56,000/- per year.

The claims tribunal, according to the appellant,
has not considered the aspect that after the accident the appellant is not able to continue in service.
5. He further submits that the claims tribunal has considered the permanent disability of the appellant to the extent of 10%.

He submits that this conclusion of the claims tribunal is not correct in view of the statement of treating doctor of the appellant, Dr. Ashish Mehrotra AW-3 who has stated before the claims tribunal that appellant has sustained 45% permanent disability, the certificate of permanent disability was exhibited as Ex.P-12.

He submits that even after 45%
permanent disability of both the legs, the claims tribunal has considered 10% over all disability Sunil vs Rajkumar Singh on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53112911/
1 which is not correct and proper.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. He also submits that nothing has been awarded for loss of amenities and for loss of marriage proposal because the appellant was 22 years of age at the time of accident.

He has certainly suffered because of accident in as much as he would not be getting marriage proposals, he would have got, if 3 MA-3189-2024 he had not suffered permanent disability in his both legs to the extent of 45%.
He thus submits that the compensation should be enhanced substantially.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the extent of permanent disability of the appellant.

By referring to the findings in para 13 of the award has stated that it has clearly been admitted by Dr. Ashish Mehrorta AW-3 that the appellant has suffered 20% permanent disability with respect to over all body.
He also submits that the claims tribunal has correctly taken the income of the appellant and awarded proper sum as compensation, thus, no interference is warranted with the impugned award.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
It is undisputable from the facts as recorded in the award that the appellant has sustained several and serious grievous injuries on different parts of his body.
Both of his legs got fractures and he remained under treatment for a very long period.
Dr. Ashish Mehrotra has clearly stated in his statement as AW-3 that the appellant has suffered 45% permanent disability in both of his legs.
He also stated that certificate of permanent disability in this regard has been issued by medical board.

The said certificate is exhibited as Ex.P-12.
10.

In view of the fact that the appellant has suffered 45% permanent disability in both of his legs and also considering that AW-3 Dr. Ashish Mehrotra has also stated in his cross-examination with respect to over all body the appellant has suffered 20% permanent disability.

It would be proper 4 MA-3189-2024 to consider permanent disability of the appellant at 20% instead of 10%.
11.
As regards the income of the appellant, no fault is found in the same.
As regards, the submission of the appellant that nothing has been awarded for loss of marriage proposal and loss of amenities though should have been granted.
It appears reasonable to consider that certainly after sustaining permanent disability in both of his legs, the appellant is deprived from several amenities of life.

Thus, keeping in view the fact that by assessing the permanent disability of the appellant at 10%, the claims tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.3,93,122/- in the head of permanent disability (to be clear a total compensation of RS.12,05,000/- has been awarded).
12.
This Court considers it proper to award further lump-sum amount of Rs.4 Lacs over and above the amount which has already been awarded by the claims tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for further amount of Rs.4 Lacs over and above the amount which has already been awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% from the date of the application.
13. With the aforesaid, present appeal stands disposed of.
